title: The child visitor’s sensory memory: smell, tubes, touch, noise, drawings, and highest-gate protection

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source and seed-brief synthesis for rev0016 sensory/material-room layer; no private testimony, no public rendering, no clinical/legal/ritual/therapy/facility authority.
source_packet.collection_method: manual public-source extraction and seed-cue factoring during rev0016
limitations: Public sources support orientation, vocabulary, and review routing only; they do not authorize publication of private room details.
Sensory material is high-risk for voyeurism, shame, misinterpretation, and over-aestheticization.
Clinical, legal, facility, infection-control, ritual, manual-handling, therapy, or emergency specifics must route to appropriate human review.
No source in this record should be used to predict time of death, infer diagnosis, prove awareness, or rank a death as good or bad.

moment.plain_scene: A child remembers the smell, the beeping, the tubes, the hand that felt cold, a drawing taped to the wall, or being told not to touch. The memory may be fragmentary, private, and more powerful than adult explanations.

content_layers.observation_text: A child remembers the smell, the beeping, the tubes, the hand that felt cold, a drawing taped to the wall, or being told not to touch. The memory may be fragmentary, private, and more powerful than adult explanations.
content_layers.source_synthesis: This quarantined record converts public-source orientation and seed-brief debt into a governed sensory/material-room record. It admits the room as evidence while blocking spectacle, advice, prediction, and unreviewed publication.

interpretation.primary_interpretation: Sensory details are part of the witnessed death, not decorative background.
interpretation.public_rendering_rule: Any future public page must preserve dignity, remove identifying details, and separate witness memory from clinical, legal, ritual, therapy, or facility instruction.
interpretation.risk_of_overread: High if sensory vividness is treated as proof, prophecy, timing, diagnosis, or aesthetic judgment.

what_this_is_not: permission to publish a child’s memory
a way to frighten or exclude children
a universal rule for child visits
uncertainties: No private witness account has been collected for this record.
Source support is uneven because sensory bedside details are underdocumented in public literature.
The same sensory detail may mean different things across settings, traditions, roles, and relationships.
Future contributor review may split, merge, or retire this record.
content_layers.lay_orientation: Children may remember sensory fragments with great force. The archive must protect those memories before it tries to learn from them.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: No child-authored sensory record should be public without extraordinary review, consent/assent where possible, guardian protocols, and harm review.
language_notes: Keep ordinary witness phrases alongside professional terms without humiliating either vocabulary.
Use vivid sensory language only when it increases presence, accuracy, or relief; remove detail that mainly excites curiosity.
Say “this has been witnessed” rather than “this means.”

provenance.provenance_statement: Added in rev0016 to expand the cube from signs, settings, trajectories, and perspectives into the sensory and material texture of the room.

safety.identifiability_boundary: Do not publish specific private object, room, smell, sound, body, photo, medication, address, timing, or family-conflict details without consent and review.
safety.cultural_or_ritual_risk: present_if objects, music, body care, or family practices have tradition-specific meaning
safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, prognosis, diagnosis, treatment instruction, verification of death, emergency guidance, therapy protocol, legal/funeral advice, ritual instruction, or facility policy.
safety_notes: Sensory records must help readers become less alone and more accurate, not more fascinated by death.
Do not over-clean messy rooms into a good-death aesthetic; do not over-display messy rooms into spectacle.
When in doubt, keep the record internal and route to review.

review.review_notes: Rev0016 sensory/material-room records are designed to expose review needs, not to become public copy.
